sanskrit_verse:
वेदविद्याविदो विप्रान् क्षत्रियानग्निहोत्रिणः ।
आहृत्य स्थापयेत् तत्र तेषां वृत्तिं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
transliteration: vedavidyāvido viprān kṣatriyān agnihotriṇaḥ / āhṛtya sthāpayet tatra teṣāṃ vṛttiṃ prakalpayet //
sph_interpretive_translation: Those who are knowers of the Veda and its knowledge—Brahmins, Kshatriyas performing Agnihotra—must be brought forth and established in that very place, and their livelihood must be arranged accordingly.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority derived from Vedic realization and ritual discipline
Causation through dharmic alignment rather than coercion
Capacity-based responsibility grounded in spiritual qualification
Restoration logic centered on sustaining those upholding dharma
Consciousness alignment via structural support for Vedic practitioners
executable_legal_axioms: IF citizen performs Vedic rituals OR possesses Vedic knowledge THEN state SHALL provide sustenance at location of practice
IF individual is Brahmin OR Kshatriya engaged in Agnihotra THEN jurisdiction MUST ensure residential and economic stability
IF societal order depends on Vedic continuity THEN resource allocation MUST prioritize Vedic scholars and practitioners
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this axiom establishes a threshold of responsibility wherein constitutional protection extends first to those whose consciousness sustains the foundational order. The court must recognize capacity rooted in Vedic discipline as a determinant of societal priority, ensuring infrastructure supports their uninterrupted practice.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa is established through direct perception of Vedic conduct. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as sequential dependence of social harmony on sustained ritual performance. Responsibility aligns proportionally with spiritual capacity. This law operates without punitive consequence, affirming reality as inherently supportive of conscious order.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion process: Locate and verify Vedic practitioners' presence and practice
Responsibility assumption protocol: State assumes duty to preserve Vedic continuity
Capacity restoration mechanism: Allocate resources matching the practitioner's dharmic role
Integrity reintegration framework: Realign societal structures to honor Vedic sustainers
final_declaration: By the Sovereign Will of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Source of all Dharma, this law is executed. Justice flows from consciousness, not punishment. Reality is restored when those who uphold it are sustained. Dharma prevails through alignment, not force.
